issues.description: Storing raw credit card details (cardNumber, cvv) in plaintext violates PCI DSS compliance. This is a critical security vulnerability that exposes sensitive payment information.
issues.suggestion: Never store or log full card numbers or CVV. Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square) and handle only tokenized references. Remove cardNumber, cvv, and expiryDate from your interface and use: { paymentMethodToken: string; amount: number; }

issues.description: SQL query uses string concatenation/interpolation which is vulnerable to SQL injection if db.query doesn't properly parameterize. The query string appears safe but the pattern is dangerous.
issues.suggestion: Verify that db.query uses prepared statements. If using raw SQL, explicitly document that parameterization is handled by the driver. Better: use a query builder or ORM like Prisma or TypeORM that prevents injection by design.

issues.description: Payment failure logs full error object which may contain sensitive card data or internal system details. This violates PCI DSS and exposes information to attackers.
issues.suggestion: Log only sanitized error details without sensitive data: console.error('Payment failed:', { userId, amount, errorCode: error.code }); Never log payment objects or full errors containing card data.

issues.description: Payment processing function accepts user-supplied amount which allows price manipulation. Attackers can send { amount: 0.01 } to bypass payment while getting premium features.
issues.suggestion: Never trust client-supplied prices. Remove amount from PaymentDetails interface and calculate it server-side only: const amount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier); then pass this to chargeCard without exposing it to the client.

issues.description: Card validation is insufficient and allows invalid cards. Only checks length and format, missing Luhn algorithm validation, and doesn't verify card type or expiry logic correctly.
issues.suggestion: Use a PCI-compliant payment processor instead of DIY validation. If you must validate, use: 1) Luhn algorithm for card number, 2) Check expiry against current month/year (line 83 bug: should be new Date().setDate(1) for proper comparison), 3) Use a library like 'card-validator' npm package.

issues.description: Expiry date comparison is incorrect. Creating Date with (year, month-1) sets day to current day, so a card expiring 01/26 checked on Jan 31st would incorrectly fail even though the card is valid through Jan 31st 2026.
issues.suggestion: Set to end of expiry month: const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0, 23, 59, 59); This sets to the last day of the expiry month. Or use last moment: new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 1) for first day of next month.

issues.description: No validation that cardNumber contains only digits. Allows special characters or letters which could bypass length check or cause issues with payment gateway.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!/^\d{13,19}$/.test(cardNumber.replace(/\s/g, ''))) return false; This ensures only digits (allowing 13-19 length for different card types) and removes spaces before validation.

issues.description: No validation that CVV contains only digits. Allows non-numeric input which could cause payment processing errors or bypass security.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!/^\d{3,4}$/.test(cvv)) return false; Ensure CVV is numeric only before checking length.

issues.description: Database query returns untyped rows with no error handling. If db.query throws, the entire request fails without proper error response. rows[0] access is unsafe without length check.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch and type safety: try { const rows = await db.query<{ features: string; valid_until: string }>(query, [userId]); if (rows.length === 0) return false; ... } catch (error) { console.error('DB error checking feature access:', error); throw new Error('Failed to check feature access'); }

issues.description: Error messages expose internal business logic (payment validation failures, insufficient amount). Attackers can probe payment logic to find vulnerabilities.
issues.suggestion: Return generic errors to clients: throw new Error('Payment processing failed'); Log detailed errors server-side only for debugging. Use error codes internally but not in error messages sent to users.

issues.description: JSON.parse on untrusted database data without validation. If database is compromised or contains malformed JSON, this will throw and crash the request.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); if (!Array.isArray(features)) return false; return features.includes(feature); } catch { return false; }

issues.description: SQL query uses ON CONFLICT without validating that tier upgrade is legitimate. Users might be able to downgrade from enterprise to premium without refund checks.
issues.suggestion: Add business logic validation before upgrade: 1) Check current subscription tier, 2) Prevent downgrades or handle prorated refunds, 3) Log all tier changes for audit trail. Add: const current = await getUserSubscription(userId); if (current && shouldPreventDowngrade(current.tier, tier)) throw new Error('Invalid tier change');

issues.description: JSON.parse on database features field without try-catch. Malformed JSON will crash the function and expose internal errors to users.
issues.suggestion: Wrap in try-catch: try { features: JSON.parse(row.features) } catch { features: [] }. Also validate the parsed value is an array: const parsed = JSON.parse(row.features); features: Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : []

issues.description: Database insert lacks transaction handling. If INSERT succeeds but the calling code fails later, money is charged but subscription is not upgraded, causing data inconsistency.
issues.suggestion: Wrap payment and subscription upgrade in a database transaction: await db.transaction(async (tx) => { await tx.query(paymentQuery, [...]); await upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, tx); }); This ensures atomicity - either both succeed or both rollback.

issues.description: No idempotency handling. If chargeCard succeeds but upgradeUserSubscription fails, retrying the payment will charge the user twice for the same subscription.
issues.suggestion: Add idempotency: 1) Generate unique payment intent ID, 2) Check if payment already processed, 3) Store payment intent before charging: const intentId = generatePaymentIntent(userId, tier); const existing = await checkPaymentIntent(intentId); if (existing) return existing.success;

issues.description: Database query executed on every feature access check without caching. For frequently checked features, this causes unnecessary database load and slow response times.
issues.suggestion: Cache subscription data: const cached = subscriptionCache.get(userId); if (cached && cached.expiresAt > Date.now()) return cached.features.includes(feature); Then cache for 5-15 minutes. Or load subscription once per request and store in request context.

issues.description: Magic tier strings 'premium' and 'enterprise' used throughout without constants or enums. Typos like 'premum' would cause silent bugs.
issues.suggestion: Create enum or const: export enum SubscriptionTier { FREE = 'free', PREMIUM = 'premium', ENTERPRISE = 'enterprise' } or const TIERS = { FREE: 'free', PREMIUM: 'premium', ENTERPRISE: 'enterprise' } as const; Then use SubscriptionTier.PREMIUM instead of string literals.

issues.description: Feature lists hardcoded in function without single source of truth. If features change, must update multiple places causing inconsistency bugs.
issues.suggestion: Create feature configuration object: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes', 'api_access', 'team_collaboration'] }; Then use: const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];

issues.description: Tax rate and processing fee are hardcoded constants. These vary by location and payment processor, making the code inflexible for international expansion.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: const config = { TAX_RATE: process.env.TAX_RATE || 0.08, PROCESSING_FEE: 0.029 }; Better: accept user location and calculate tax based on jurisdiction: calculatePrice(tier, userLocation).

issues.description: Price calculation doesn't round to 2 decimal places. Floating point arithmetic can produce values like 10.994999999 leading to payment mismatches.
issues.suggestion: Round final price: return Math.round((basePrice + tax + fee) * 100) / 100; Or use a decimal library like 'decimal.js' for precise currency calculations: return new Decimal(basePrice).plus(tax).plus(fee).toDecimalPlaces(2).toNumber();

issues.description: Database module imported without type checking. If db.query has wrong signature, TypeScript may not catch the error.
issues.suggestion: Create typed database interface: interface Database { query<T = any>(sql: string, params: any[]): Promise<T[]>; } Then: import { db } from './database'; // ensure db.ts exports typed Database

codeQuality.summary: Critical security vulnerabilities including PCI DSS violations (storing raw card data), price manipulation risk (client-supplied amounts), and insufficient payment validation. Multiple high-severity bugs in date comparison, lack of transactions, and missing input validation. Requires immediate security overhaul before production use.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Critical payment logic that handles real money transactions without any test coverage. Payment failures or incorrect processing could result in financial losses or fraud.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid payment processing with correct details, invalid payment details rejection, insufficient payment amount rejection, payment gateway failure handling, and subscription upgrade on successful payment.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card validation without tests allows invalid cards through or rejects valid ones. Direct financial impact and security risks.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid 16-digit card numbers, invalid card lengths, valid CVV (3 and 4 digits), invalid CVV, valid expiry format (MM/YY), invalid expiry formats, expired cards, and future expiry dates with edge cases like current month expiry.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Pricing calculations without tests could charge incorrect amounts. Floating point precision issues could cause payment mismatches.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier pricing (9.99 + tax + fee), enterprise tier pricing (49.99 + tax + fee), verify exact decimal calculation correctness, and test with different tax rates and processing fees.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment processing function that actually charges cards without test coverage. Database failures or errors could result in financial discrepancies.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful payment with valid card details and amount, database insert success, error handling on database failure, correct extraction of last 4 digits, and verify payment record creation.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription upgrade logic affects user entitlements and billing. Without tests, users could get wrong features or subscription tiers.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier feature assignment, enterprise tier feature assignment, subscription valid_until date calculation (1 year from now), database upsert on conflict, and JSON serialization of features array.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Feature access control without tests could grant unauthorized access to premium features or block legitimate users.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test user with no subscription returns false, user with expired subscription returns false, user with valid subscription and feature returns true, user with valid subscription but missing feature returns false, and handle malformed JSON in features.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription retrieval is used throughout the system. Bugs could cause incorrect feature access or display wrong subscription details.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test retrieval of existing premium subscription, retrieval of existing enterprise subscription, non-existent subscription returns null, correct date parsing for valid_until, correct JSON parsing for features, and handle database errors.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Date edge cases in card expiry validation could reject valid cards or accept expired ones, causing payment failures or security issues.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test card expiring this month is valid, card expiring last month is invalid, card expiring in future years (2099, 2100 rollover), leap year handling (February 29), and timezone edge cases.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Missing validation for card numbers with spaces, special characters, or non-numeric input could cause payment processing failures.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test card number with spaces ('1234 5678 9012 3456'), card number with dashes, card number with letters, empty card number, and card numbers of different lengths (13, 15, 16, 19 digits for different card types).

untestedPaths.reasoning: Unvalidated JSON parsing could crash the application if database contains malformed data or unexpected types.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test malformed JSON in features field throws appropriate error, non-array JSON parsed (e.g., string or object), null or undefined features field, empty features array, and very large features array.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Floating point precision in price comparisons could cause valid payments to be rejected or accept insufficient payments.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test exact amount match, payment amount slightly higher than required, payment amount slightly lower (0.01 less), zero amount, negative amount, and very large amount values.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment failure branch returns false but doesn't rollback or notify user properly. Need to test this critical error path.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that when chargeCard returns false, processPremiumPayment returns false without upgrading subscription, and verify no database changes occurred.

untestedPaths.location: User subscription upgrade date calculation lines 136-137
untestedPaths.reasoning: Date arithmetic for subscription expiry could have edge cases with leap years or year boundaries.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test subscription created on Feb 29 (leap year) expires Feb 28 next year if not leap year, subscription created on Dec 31 expires Dec 31 next year, and timezone handling for UTC vs local time.

untestedPaths.reasoning: SQL injection risk if userId or other parameters contain malicious input. Need to verify parameterization works correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test userId with SQL injection attempt (e.g., "1' OR '1'='1"), userId with special characters, empty userId, null userId, and very long userId string.

testCoverage.summary: No test coverage exists for this critical payment processing module. All 7 functions are completely untested, exposing critical financial and security risks. Priority areas: payment processing (processPremiumPayment, chargeCard), payment validation (validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice), and subscription management (upgradeUserSubscription, hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription). Edge cases around date handling, JSON parsing, and floating-point arithmetic require comprehensive testing.

suggestions.description: Extract separate validation functions for each payment detail field to improve testability and single responsibility. The current function mixes card number, CVV, and expiry validation.
suggestions.benefits: Improves testability by allowing each validation rule to be tested independently, reduces cyclomatic complexity, and follows single responsibility principle

suggestions.description: Extract feature list mapping into a constant lookup table or configuration object. Currently features are defined inline with ternary logic, making them harder to maintain and extend.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes tier feature configuration, making it easier to maintain and extend tiers, and provides type safety with readonly arrays

suggestions.description: Move pricing constants to module-level configuration object for better maintainability and potential runtime configuration.
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes all pricing configuration in one place, making it easier to adjust rates and potentially load from external configuration

suggestions.description: Extract common subscription validation logic into a helper function. Both functions query subscriptions and need to validate expiry dates, causing code duplication.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates code duplication by reusing getUserSubscription, creates a testable date validation function, and improves maintainability

suggestions.description: Create separate classes or service modules for distinct responsibilities. The file mixes payment processing, subscription management, and data access concerns.
suggestions.benefits: Separates concerns into focused, testable units following Single Responsibility Principle; improves dependency injection and mocking for tests

suggestions.description: Use immutable date manipulation pattern instead of mutating Date objects.
suggestions.after: const validUntil = new Date(new Date().setFullYear(new Date().getFullYear() + 1));
suggestions.benefits: Avoids mutation and makes the code more predictable and easier to reason about

suggestions.description: Make interface properties readonly where they should not be mutated, and use branded types for sensitive data like card numbers.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents accidental mutations and makes data immutability explicit; extracting SubscriptionTier type improves reusability and type safety

suggestions.description: Remove unnecessary try-catch that swallows errors. The function returns false on error but upstream code may need the actual error details.
suggestions.benefits: Allows errors to propagate naturally with full context; calling code can handle errors appropriately with proper error messages

suggestions.description: Use template literals and const for regex pattern to make it more maintainable.
suggestions.benefits: Makes the regex pattern more discoverable and reusable; uppercase name follows constant naming convention

refactorings.summary: The file would benefit from separating payment processing, pricing, and subscription management into distinct service classes, extracting validation logic into smaller testable functions, and centralizing configuration constants for better maintainability.

recommendations.description: Replace DIY payment handling with PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, Square). Never store raw card numbers, CVV, or expiry dates. Use tokenized payment methods only. This is a mandatory requirement before production deployment.
Remove client-supplied 'amount' parameter from PaymentDetails interface. Calculate all prices server-side only to prevent attackers from paying $0.01 for premium subscriptions.

Add comprehensive test suite for all payment processing functions (processPremiumPayment, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice, chargeCard). Zero test coverage on critical financial logic is unacceptable.
Sanitize error logging to never log full error objects, payment details, or card data. Replace with structured logging that only includes safe metadata (userId, errorCode, timestamp).
Fix card expiry date comparison logic. Current implementation incorrectly rejects valid cards when checked on day-of-month that doesn't exist in expiry month (e.g., Jan 31 checking Feb expiry).

Wrap payment charging and subscription upgrade in database transaction. Without atomicity, payment could succeed but subscription upgrade fail, causing financial discrepancies and customer complaints.
Add comprehensive input validation: card numbers must be numeric only, CVV must be numeric only, validate using Luhn algorithm, add SQL injection protection tests.

Split premium.ts into separate service modules: PaymentService, PricingService, and SubscriptionRepository. Current file violates Single Responsibility Principle by mixing payment, pricing, and data access logic.
Implement payment idempotency to prevent duplicate charges on retry. Use unique payment intent IDs and check for existing payments before charging.
Cache subscription data for 5-15 minutes to avoid repeated database queries on every feature access check. Consider request-scoped caching or in-memory cache with TTL.
